newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate dips 80 bps to 10.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate dips 80 bps to 10.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate dipped 80 basis points to 10.8 percent on Monday amid good supply as banks also borrowed money from the central bank.
Settlements totalled a handsome 73.4 million kuna, leaving some 10 million surplus in supply. But demand for 3.5 million in term funds was not met as lenders offered mostly call money.
Fresh borrowing was strong at 55.6 million kuna and the rest were old loans rolled over by creditors.
Interbank call money stood at a stable 10.5 percent.
Two-week rates ranged between 10.5 and 13.5 percent with one-month money at 15 and 16 percent.
Insurers' reissued one-week credits at an unchanged 9.0 percent rate.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday stronger at 6.0185 versus the dollar and weaker at 3.5716 against the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
